summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for acute decompensated heart failure with worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, and lower extremity edema, with a 7 kg weight gain since his last discharge. He developed transient hypotension likely due to accidental doubling of his home medications, which resolved without intervention. He was treated with intravenous Lasix, later transitioned to oral Lasix 160 mg daily, achieving a discharge weight of 79.9 kg with improved symptoms. His INR dropped to 1.7, prompting bridging with heparin and warfarin dose adjustment to 3 mg daily. Metoprolol was restarted at 12.5 mg daily once blood pressure stabilized. Glyburide was held inpatient with transition to sliding scale insulin; atorvastatin and vitamin D were initiated. He was discharged home with home health services and follow-up in the heart failure clinic, with instructions to monitor weight and maintain anticoagulation.
